verdict.line: You lose if you let him farm Parrrley pokes freely before level 6; you win if you survive to force all-ins while his Remove Scurvy is down.

brief.thesis: Gangplank's Parrrley (Q, 625 range, 5s CD) out-ranges both your Thundering Smash (300 range) and Frenzied Maul (325 range), so every early trade he initiates is free unless you answer with Sky Splitter. His Grog-Soaked Blade poison stacks on every auto he lands, which is why the raw lane numbers favor him even though solo kills are dead even — this is a lane you survive on cooldown-tracking, not raw stats, before you flip it with your own burst.

theirWindow.when: You're in his 625-range Q, E down
theirWindow.what: He free-pokes with Parrrley and stacks Grog-Soaked Blade poison with zero retaliation risk. Hold minions at a sane position and don't walk up to trade until your E (Sky Splitter, 16s CD) is ready to answer at range.

yourWindow.when: His W (18-22s CD) is on cooldown
yourWindow.what: Remove Scurvy clears any CC on him, so a Q (Thundering Smash) stun into a full combo is wasted if he can just cleanse and heal through it. Only commit the Q-stun into double-W into R when his W is confirmed down — that's the only time your CC actually locks him in place.

boots.why: 53.5% over 275 games. Lower ability haste means your 12-10s Q and 16s E come back faster, so you can re-threaten the stun sooner after he burns Remove Scurvy to cleanse it.

runes.keystoneWhy: Ramping attack speed in sustained combat stacks with your passive's attack-speed grant and your double-tap W combo, so once you force him into melee range you out-trade his hit-and-run poison stacks instead of losing the war of attrition.

summoners.why: This combo measures at 50.3% over its sample, the best of the three options. Exhaust directly answers his kiting Parrrley pattern — it slows him so your Q can actually land and cuts his damage during the all-in window when his W is down.

playing.title: Poke back with E, don't walk up
playing.detail: Sky Splitter has 1200 range, far beyond his Parrrley's 625 — use it to answer his pokes at distance instead of eating free damage while closing in.

playing.title: Track his W before committing Q
playing.detail: Remove Scurvy clears your stun and heals him, so don't burn Thundering Smash into a full combo unless his 18-22s cooldown W is confirmed down.

playing.title: Always double-tap your W
playing.detail: Frenzied Maul's second cast on the same marked target deals bonus damage and heals you — this is your main sustain tool to outlast his poison poke.

playing.title: Punish his auto-reset habits
playing.detail: Q grants speed toward the first enemy you attack and stuns them, so the moment he steps up to land an auto, dash in and lock him down.

playing.title: Play passive before level 6
playing.detail: Your kit has no answer to his range advantage until E is ranked and R is live, so hold waves and avoid unnecessary trades through levels 1-5.

playing.title: Use R to disable towers, not just damage
playing.detail: Stormbringer's landing temporarily disables nearby enemy towers, turning your level 6-8 power spike into a split-push or dive tool, not just an all-in.

playing.title: Itemize into his poison stacking
playing.detail: Randuin's Omen and Spirit Visage both blunt Grog-Soaked Blade's stacking magic damage, so prioritize them if the poison keeps swinging trades his way.

brief.patchCaveat: The build, runes, boots, summoner spells, and win-rate figures above come from measured games on the current patch via OP.GG. The tactical reasoning — why each pick answers Gangplank's kit specifically — is my own read, not sourced data.
